items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1960-01-16
items.q: Him and George, your boy, and they had a swinging little old band around there, you know.

ctx.x: Would it be 1900 or would it be 1910 or 1920 or what?

No, I don't think it was that far back. That's it. Dewey used to wait on Basin Street, Emmanuel Perez. That's when I was very small. Yeah, that must bring back. Let's see, wait, I got to get that thing straight. I think Tom could tell you better than I could about that. Tom Alba? Yeah. Because I had learned how to play cornet, you know, and Tom was playing the violin. And Eddie Vincent was practicing every day with us. And then all at once he picked up and he left there with Jimmy Fallon and then we went north.…

items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1959-12-09
items.q: Williams' brother played the bass in the band and George Lewis.

ctx.x: office. Well yes you told me about that once you had your own band. That's the time Clarence

Williams' brother played the bass in the band and George Lewis. A fella in the name of Buddy Brunson. That man had the funniest lip I ever seen. I don't know what kind of trombone that he had. An E flat tenor trombone or something. A high one, a little one. Yeah. With the valve. With the valve. And he didn't know even how to tune but he could play it. You know what he'd do? He'd sound the air on the violin you know. And he'd finger any one of them valves, and he'd be flat that way he'd blow it up. He'd say, and…
I want to ask a little bit about Vincent again. How did he play? Did he ever take the slide trombone later? Do you remember?
